issues.legal_issue: A reversioner has no present right to apportionment of compensation for acquired property while the limited-owner widow is alive.
material_facts: The claimant sought apportionment of compensation for acquired property as the reversioner of the last male owner.
The claimant challenged an alienation made by the deceased owner's widow, who held a widow's interest in the property.
The widow was still alive when the claimant sought compensation.
issues.conclusion: The claimant was not entitled to apportionment or receipt of compensation during the widow's lifetime, whether the alienation was valid or invalid.
issues.legal_principle: A reversioner has no title in praesenti to property subject to a widow's limited interest while she is alive and therefore has no present entitlement to compensation for its acquisition. The Court relied on no statutory provision or earlier case.

predicates.acquired_property_compensation_claim: A person seeks apportionment of compensation for property acquired by the state.
predicates.claimant_is_reversioner: The person seeking compensation claims as the reversioner of a former owner.
predicates.widow_alive: The widow holding a limited interest in the property is alive when compensation is sought.

issues.definition: When a reversioner seeks compensation for acquired property while the limited-interest widow is alive, the reversioner is not entitled to compensation during her lifetime.
